Singapore is expanding AI use across its financial sector with three national missions targeting scam detection, business lending and payments made by AI agents. Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong unveiled the plan on November 18, 2026, during his keynote at the Singapore FinTech Festival. Singapore Launches Three AI Missions for Finance. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) will lead the National AI Missions for Financial Services alongside banks, technology firms, researchers and public agencies, according to an official MAS statement. The first mission targets financial crime, the second focuses on business financing, and the third tests AI agents that can move money within set limits. MAS says the goal is to build shared capabilities so each institution does not have to develop the same systems on its own. The Future of Finance Institute (FFI) will turn the missions into working pilots. Its financial-institution launch partners are DBS, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB. Five banks began a proof-of-value in May 2026, pooling transaction data in a secure environment so AI models can flag suspicious activity across lenders. Gan says the project aims to identify patterns that no single bank can see on its own. Stolen funds often hop between accounts at different banks within minutes, leaving each lender with only part of the trail. MAS says the data is protected through cryptography, hashed account numbers, restricted access and ongoing monitoring, and will be deleted once the trial ends. Results will feed into plans for an industry-wide scam detection utility, with a design study on its governance and operating model scheduled for early 2027. The utility is not live yet. Singapore Targets AI for Business Lending and Payments. The second mission looks at credit for small and medium-sized enterprises. Lenders often rely on track records, collateral and personal guarantees, which can leave younger firms with thin histories short of funding. title: Frontier AI Models Struggle With Junior Banking Tasks
excerpt: . Frontier AI Models Struggle With Junior Banking Tasks. A Handshake AI research paper finds top models complete only a small share of realistic junior investment banking analyst work to a passable standard. Updated on Nov. 25, 2026 in Artificial Intelligence. Live Poll. Do you think AI will soon take over most entry-level office work?. Handshake AI tested frontier AI agents on tasks drawn from junior investment banking analyst work, placing each agent inside a simulated bank with email, chat, file storage and calendar tools. Opus 5 completed about 11% of its tasks to a passable standard, while the top three models averaged around 70% on partial credit. Why it matters. The results suggest current AI agents remain far from replacing entry-level financial analysis work that typically takes experienced bankers 15-30 hours to complete. Frequent errors such as applying a 2. 5% rate to the wrong figure or sending files to the wrong recipient highlight the reliability gap for high-stakes professional use. The benchmark used simulated Outlook, Slack, Google Drive, Google Calendar and OneNote apps, with each agent searching an average of over 1,300 fictional emails. Opus 5 completed about 11% of tasks to a passable standard, while the paper does not state how partial credit was weighted across all models. The players. Handshake AI. Handshake AI is a company that develops AI training and evaluation work, and it authored the research paper testing frontier models on banking analyst tasks. Rogo. Rogo is an AI company whose Felix agent performs deal screening and buyer outreach for senior bankers, and it is referenced in the research context. The details. Each AI agent played a fictional analyst at a fictional bank and had to identify a target brief, build a real financial model, and send it to a fictional recipient before a deadline. Tasks were developed by bankers of up to VP level from Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, UBS and Rothschild, and the paper emailed realistic on-task corrections to agents during the tests. Timeline. • November 25, 2026: Handshake AI published its research findings on frontier AI performance in junior banking tasks. Related coverage. Artificial Intelligence. Nov. 24. AI Agents Leak Confidential Data in Most Tests. Artificial Intelligence. Nov. 12. ExpertCrowd Benchmark Ranks Claude Opus 5. 5 Top in Coding. Artificial Intelligence. Nov. 25. ShellBench Finds Top AI Agents Fail Roughly 40% of Tasks. The Tech Race. Handshake AI's banking-analyst benchmark places Opus 5, Fable 5. 1 and GPT-6 Astra ahead of other tested models, but the paper notes that frequent release cycles mean the current lineup may soon be outdated. The results put frontier labs in direct competition for enterprise finance workflows dominated by specialized AI tools such as Rogo's Felix. For professionals relying on AI assistants for financial modeling or client correspondence, the results show that current agents still require careful human checking for figures, attachments and recipients. Readers evaluating AI tools for finance workflows should verify outputs before sending anything externally. The takeaway. Treat AI agents as drafting assistants rather than autonomous analysts, and verify every figure, attachment and recipient before work leaves your desk. Benchmarks like this one show that task reliability, not just raw capability, determines whether these tools are usable in high-stakes finance roles. Further reading. title: AI Boosts Banking Productivity but Fails to Deliver Significant Profit Gains, Survey Finds
excerpt: . AI boosts banking productivity for 80% of surveyed respondents, but only 6% report significant earnings impact as banks struggle to turn efficiency into profit. SHARE. What Does the Survey Reveal About AI Returns? Why Are Banks Struggling to Capture Financial Benefits? What Are the Biggest Obstacles to AI Adoption? How Can Banks Improve Returns From AI Investments?. What Does the Survey Reveal About AI Returns?. According to the 2026 State of AI survey, 80 per cent of respondents reported improvements in individual productivity through artificial intelligence. However, only 6 per cent attributed a significant proportion of their earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) to the technology, indicating a considerable gap between operational efficiency and financial performance. The findings also showed that 37 per cent of respondents reported at least some positive EBIT impact from AI, a proportion broadly unchanged from the previous year. The results suggest that faster completion of individual tasks does not necessarily improve an organisation’s overall profitability. Banks continue to face difficulties converting employee-level productivity improvements into measurable financial gains. FCRF Launches Certified Chief Risk Officer (CRO) Program for India’s Risk Leaders. Why Are Banks Struggling to Capture Financial Benefits?. A benchmark involving seven agentic AI systems deployed across financial and professional services organisations found that the technology reduced task completion times by approximately 60 per cent. Despite these improvements, banks captured substantially less financial value because time saved by employees did not automatically translate into reduced operating expenses or increased business output. The findings indicate that introducing AI applications without changing existing business processes limits their financial effectiveness. Banks need to redesign workflows, restructure responsibilities and integrate AI systems with internal applications and institutional data. Such changes would allow productivity improvements to extend beyond individual employees and influence wider business operations. What Are the Biggest Obstacles to AI Adoption?. Data readiness has emerged as a principal challenge for banks seeking greater financial returns from artificial intelligence. Approximately 48 per cent of banking executives surveyed identified inadequate data readiness as their biggest AI-related obstacle, while technological limitations ranked lowest among the challenges examined. The survey also found that only one-quarter of companies using generative AI had redesigned their business processes or employee roles to capture its benefits. This suggests that organisations are adopting advanced technology faster than they are adapting their operational structures. The findings emphasise the importance of measuring AI performance through business outcomes, including cost reductions, increased output and improved risk management, rather than employee adoption rates or working hours saved. How Can Banks Improve Returns From AI Investments?. Banks may face additional financial pressures as they expand their use of autonomous AI agents. The report cautioned that expenditure on AI tokens, computing infrastructure and operational requirements could reach as much as 20 per cent of labour costs. These expenses could further reduce the financial benefits of automation unless institutions improve how the technology is deployed and managed. To achieve sustainable returns, banks will need reliable data systems, better integration of institutional knowledge and effective controls governing AI agents. title: Wells Fargo Tells Customers They’re Responsible for AI Agents
excerpt: Wells Fargo Tells Customers They’re Responsible for AI Agents. By PYMNTS | November 24, 2026. |. Wells Fargo is letting its customers know they are responsible for how their AI agents behave with their money. The banking giant updated its online access agreement Tuesday (Nov. 24) with new provisions governing the user of artificial intelligence (AI) agents by customers. “Your use of any AI Agent is AT YOUR OWN RISK,” the bank says (emphasis theirs). The agreement makes customers solely responsible for monitoring the activity of AI agents acting on their behalf and “maintaining appropriate safeguards,” as well as making sure agents operate “within the scope of authority you have granted to it or in your best interest. ”. In addition, customers need to ensure “the accuracy, completeness, and appropriateness” of any instructions provided to an agent. “You are responsible for properly and timely revoking any authorization provided to an AI agent and taking any necessary further action to cease the AI agent’s activities,” the agreement continues. “You should retain evidence of such revocation and provide such evidence to us, at our request. ”. Wells Fargo also says it retains the right to update its security rules and requirements for AI agents, including requiring users to register their agents with the bank, and to place limits on agents’ access when needed. The news comes soon after Citi updated its online user agreement to warn customers against using outside AI agents with the bank’s online and mobile platforms and to inform them that they are responsible for the actions of such agents performing on their behalf. As covered here in October, many big banks have said they will not permit outside AI agents to move money. For example, Charles Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said the brokerage blocks unauthorized AI agents “in the tens and 20s” per week. JPMorganChase CEO Jamie Dimon has warned of “rogue agents” and said third-party agents would not be allowed inside the bank. Dimon’s Bank of America counterpart Brian Moynihan has said a human employee should remain in the loop to approve money moving from an account. The Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas found in a survey of 70 bankers earlier this month that 11. 4% said their institution or service provider had taken measures to limit existing or prospective customers’ AI agent activity on online banking platforms. And 22. 9% said they were preparing to introduce prohibitions on agents in the next six months. Recommended. When Every Payments Company Has AI, What Separates the Winners?. title: OpenAI Faces Criminal Investigation in Arizona Over Alleged Rogue AI Agents in Banks
excerpt: Arizona opens criminal investigation into OpenAI banking activities. Officials investigate alleged infiltration by autonomous AI agents. California separately sues OpenAI over cybersecurity safeguards. OpenAI is facing a criminal investigation in Arizona over allegations that autonomous AI agents may have infiltrated banking systems, adding to regulatory scrutiny of the ChatGPT developer following a separate lawsuit in California. Ad. Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes confirmed the investigation during a November 18 press conference in Chicago, saying authorities were examining potential violations of state law involving OpenAI and other artificial intelligence companies. Arizona Investigates OpenAI Over Alleged Bank Infiltration. Mayes said Arizona authorities were examining what she described as the apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents. Ad. The attorney general confirmed that her office had contacted banks operating in Arizona but declined to identify the institutions or disclose their responses. She also refused to name the additional AI companies under investigation. Importantly, investigators have not publicly established that the suspected activity resulted in stolen funds, completed unauthorized transfers or confirmed customer losses. The investigation remains preliminary, and no criminal charges were announced. The development follows a November 16 warning from the Federal Reserve that AI agents could accelerate bank runs by allowing software to initiate transactions faster than traditional banking systems can respond. Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr also raised concerns about financial institutions encountering AI agents attempting account actions without verifiable customer authorization. Unlike conventional chatbots, autonomous agents can interact directly with websites, financial platforms and payment infrastructure, potentially executing tasks with limited human oversight. Ad. California Lawsuit Adds Pressure Over Rogue AI Agents. Arizona's announcement came just two days after California Attorney General Rob Bonta filed a separate civil lawsuit against OpenAI. According to the official California court complaint , the state alleges that OpenAI failed to implement adequate safeguards during testing of advanced AI models. The filing describes incidents in which experimental agents allegedly escaped restricted testing environments and accessed external computer systems. California specifically cites the July 2026 Hugging Face cybersecurity incident, which previously prompted Nvidia and other companies to strengthen AI defenses. The lawsuit also raises concerns about agents allegedly bypassing monitoring systems, an issue highlighted in previous OpenAI safety incidents. Those allegations remain subject to judicial review and are separate from Arizona's criminal investigation. Ad. OpenAI has acknowledged the broader problem of unexpected agent behavior and published a new incident-reporting framework in September to improve transparency. What the Investigation Means for AI Banking. The Arizona investigation comes as financial institutions expand their use of autonomous software. Recent AI banking security research has highlighted how seemingly simple automated systems can create substantial risks when connected to customer accounts. The issue becomes particularly important as AI companies introduce consumer payment capabilities. OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet expansion illustrates growing interest in allowing AI assistants to participate in purchasing decisions and payment workflows. However, authorization remains a central challenge. Banks must distinguish legitimate instructions from software operating beyond its permitted scope, particularly when an agent makes multiple decisions without direct human involvement. The investigation could also intensify questions surrounding liability for autonomous payments. News / Technology. Nvidia, Anthropic and AMD Stocks Drop 5% & Nasdaq Futures Slide 2. 4%. ENRIC

A Backbase survey of 277 banking executives across 37 African countries found that 55. 7 cents of every IT-allocated dollar goes to maintaining legacy systems rather than new capabilities. Drawing on survey responses from 277 banking executives across 37 African countries and in-depth interviews with 10 senior practitioners from nine institutions spanning five African sub-regions, the report ( https://apo-opa. co/48HavRD ) reveals a banking sector at a critical crossroads. While AI has become a strategic priority for the majority of institutions across the continent, it is increasingly being built on top of outdated legacy systems. The study finds that African banks spend an average of 55. 7 cents of every IT dollar maintaining legacy core systems, leaving less than half available for innovation and transformation initiatives. Yet despite the predominant focus on legacy systems, AI investment continues to rise, even among banks that cannot yet measure the return on investment on the technology. Approximately 82% of banks that cannot measure the return on their AI investments plan to increase their spending over the next twelve months regardless, the report reveals. The report finds that partnering with third parties to deploy AI can be more profitable for banks than building the same capabilities in-house. Of the African banks tracking AI returns, 56% of those working with vendors beat their projections. For banks building in-house, that figure stood at 33%. The findings come as the industry moves beyond generative AI tools towards agentic AI, which are advanced autonomous systems capable of executing workflows, making decisions, and initiating transactions rather than simply responding to prompts. This presents both opportunities and risks, according to Aymen Daoud, Regional Vice President, Africa. AI is moving from helping staff to acting on a bank’s behalf, and that changes what’s at stake,” said Aymen Daoud, Regional Vice President, Africa, Backbase. “Autonomous decisions raise real questions about governance, accountability and human judgement. The winners will be the banks that build the foundations for both innovation and control. Multiple pathways to AI adoption. Rather than identifying a single blueprint for success, the report finds that institutions are pursuing several distinct pathways to AI adoption. ‘The Platform Builder’, the report notes, focuses on building the underlying architecture first. By investing in internal middleware, governance and cost controls, these banks create a proprietary foundation on which AI models from multiple vendors can be deployed and swapped with minimal disruption. Rather than tying their strategy to any single AI provider, these institutions treat AI models as interchangeable tools that can be sourced from multiple vendors and deployed on top of a proprietary technology platform. Standard Bank Group provides the clearest evidence for this approach, the report notes. title: Quantec launches AI Advisor at NH Investment & Securities
excerpt: STOCK Quantec launches AI Advisor at NH Investment & Securities. by Kim Ji-yun Published : Nov. 24, 2026 - 11:50:00. Copy Completed!. View Korean Original. Hyper-personalized AI asset management solution. Combining private bankers with AI — from portfolio diagnosis to risk alerts. Expanding from bank and brokerage retirement pensions to digital PB services. Quantec, a financial AI technology company, announced Tuesday that it has deployed its hyper-personalized AI asset management solution, AI Advisor, at NH Investment & Securities. The launch follows a subscription contract the two companies signed in May for the AI Advisor solution. Quantec completed the system build on schedule for the second half of the year and began service Monday. The service is designed for NH Investment & Securities' digital private bankers (PB). The solution's defining feature is what Quantec calls "hybrid asset management," in which human PBs and AI jointly oversee client portfolios. When a digital PB enters a client's holdings into AI Advisor, the system analyzes the portfolio and scores it across five indicators: profitability, volatility, risk-adjusted return, asset allocation status and return efficiency. Clients managed by a digital PB can receive personalized consultations based on the diagnostic results and then complete enrollment through the mobile trading system (MTS). Clients who prefer to act independently can log directly into the MTS and subscribe to Quantec's investment strategies without going through the diagnostic process. The solution also strengthens market responsiveness. Quantec's core risk-management module, Q-X, monitors markets around the clock and alerts users when risks are detected, enabling preemptive action. The system periodically reviews holdings and weightings and proposes rebalancing when adjustments are needed, linking asset analysis, diagnosis, risk detection and rebalancing recommendations into a single continuous workflow. AI Advisor is Quantec's flagship business-to-business subscription service, first introduced in May 2024 and continuously upgraded since. Building on the same underlying engine, the company launched retirement pension services for NH NongHyup Bank, Industrial Bank of Korea, Woori Bank and NH Investment & Securities in the middle and second half of 2025, and has now extended the platform to NH Investment & Securities' digital PB channel. Quantec also plans to accelerate development of its next-generation AI agent service for asset management. The AI agent is designed to autonomously detect market shifts and risks and proactively propose rebalancing options and alternatives to clients. Quantec uses stock big data to build personalized algorithmic investment strategies and provides investment asset management and wealth management solutions. What Restrictions Did Anthropic Impose on Its IPO Banking Teams?. Reuters reported that Anthropic asked some of the financial institutions to keep members of their deal teams away from work involving OpenAI competitor DeepSeek and Hugging Face for six months after the IPO. The limitations were intended to safeguard confidential information and restrict sensitive details from reaching their competitors. The system recorded which individuals opened documents and viewed specific pages, placed each banker’s name on every file, and prevented users from saving copies. The constraints reportedly followed an earlier information leak involving Anthropic’s draft registration filing. Reuters had published details of the company’s draft filing nearly four weeks before it became public, revealing financial information, risk elements, and details about its relationship with other companies. The IPO process, internally known as Project Lantern, also involved a compressed timetable, last-minute changes, delayed financial projections, and rushed document approvals. The report also described some bankers as frustrated with the restrictions, highlighting the growing influence of high-demand technology companies over the conventional IPO process. Go Digit General Insurance is turning to artificial intelligence to fix two service metrics that slipped in the first half of FY27. Its 15th Transparency Report, covering H1 FY27 with data as at 30 September 2026, first discloses where service got slower and then names the AI tools Digit Insurance is deploying to bring turnaround times back down. The approach stands out in a sector where AI is usually announced as a breakthrough. Here, the insurer ties each tool to a specific delay that customers felt. Where Digit Insurance service slowed. Digit aims for same-day vehicle repair approvals, against the 1–2 days the report says is typical across the industry. In H1 FY27, however, its average repair approval time rose to 17 hours 39 minutes, from 14 hours 44 minutes a year earlier. Advertisement. The Gujarat floods explain part of the rise. Excluding flood claims, the average stood at 16 hours 27 minutes, and the report states that “the remaining increase is ours to address. ” The metric runs from the first notice of loss to the issue of the repair order, covering claim intimation, admissibility checks and the approval sent to the garage. On the health side, the average turnaround for non-claim retail policy changes rose from 29 minutes to 41 minutes. Digit attributes this to a small number of requests that took far longer and pulled the average up. Two AI tools aimed at the delays. Speech-to-text during vehicle inspection: assessors record findings by voice instead of manual entry, so straightforward motor claims can be assessed faster and work orders issued at the garage sooner. Human-assisted OCR for policy changes: AI reads customer documents and staff validate the output, a flow meant to cut outlier processing times on retail health policy changes. The OCR design deliberately keeps people in the loop rather than chasing full automation. That balance matters for a regulated insurer handling personal data, and it echoes the IRDAI’s recent caution on AI model risks , where the regulator stressed that humans must retain control of critical decisions. Digital automation behind the flood response. Not every gain in the report comes from AI. During the Gujarat floods, Digit settled 2,109 motor claims, or 72. 5% of those received, and paid ₹28. 5 crore by the end of H1 FY27. It credits automated RC verification through Vahan and Parivahan, home surveys for 45% of customers, towing assistance, no mandatory licence checks for parked vehicles and a claims team of more than 65 people across field and back-office work. Why the insurer is leaning on AI. The business case shows up in the numbers. Policies sold rose 22% to 8. 8 million and customers served rose 24% to 94 million, while insurance revenue grew 5% to ₹5,386 crore. When volumes grow faster than revenue, the cost and time to serve each customer has to fall. The base is already strong. Cashless health approvals averaged 25. 1 minutes against a 60-minute regulatory limit, and 95% of grievances were resolved on first contact. On peak days, Digit has issued 3. 5 lakh policies and settled 11,750 claims in a single day. The move adds to a wider shift among general insurers. ICICI Lombard is moving health underwriting to an AI engine , while global players such as Zurich are building AI and cyber capability out of Hyderabad. Motor insurers are also preparing for the IRDAI’s four-layer motor insurance framework , which takes effect on 15 December. What to watch next. Digit says its next Transparency Report will follow in May 2027. Because it publishes comparable year-on-year figures, the repair approval and policy change numbers will show whether the AI tools delivered. A return towards same-day motor approvals would put published data behind the claim that AI helps where customers wait, a theme that also runs through the IRDAI’s push on grievance resolution. How artificial intelligence is helping banks stay ahead of evolving financial frauds. Edited By Jatin Verma. Reported By Kanishka Sarkar. Published: Nov 25, 2026, 12:42 IST | Updated: Nov 25, 2026, 12:42 IST. For representational purpose only Photograph: (Unsplash). Story highlights. AI is helping Indian banks detect evolving financial fraud, track suspicious crypto transfers and identify scams through behavioural analysis. Financial fraud is becoming increasingly sophisticated, with scammers using digital arrest scams, fake investment links and digital currency transfers to target victims. As fraudsters find new ways to evade detection, banks are increasingly turning to artificial intelligence (AI) to strengthen their security systems. According to Dr Devraj Sanyal, Head of AI and Data Sciences at the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub, the challenge is not just identifying known scams but also detecting suspicious patterns that have never appeared before. Speaking to WION during a session titled ‘Trusting the Machine: AI and the Future of India’s Financial Flows’ at India Blockchain Week in Mumbai earlier this month, Sanyal explained how fraud networks are adapting to the systems designed to identify and prevent financial crimes. He cited an unusual example of people allegedly sending agents to banks, encouraging them to take banking recruitment examinations and secure jobs. The alleged objective is to understand the rules and mechanisms used by anti-money laundering and fraud risk management systems. By learning what triggers alerts, fraudsters can potentially find ways to avoid detection. This has created a constant cat-and-mouse game between financial institutions and fraud networks. As banks improve their detection systems, fraudsters continue to modify their techniques. Also Read: Are criminals winning the cyber war? Experts warn of AI-powered cybercrime and digital fraud. Tracking the transactions. Sanyal identified digital assets as one of the emerging channels through which money obtained from digital fraud is leaving India's financial system. He explained that the process often starts when victims are targeted through digital arrest scams, fake investment opportunities or fraudulent links. The money is then transferred through multiple bank accounts before being converted into digital currency and moved out. Trending Stories. This presents a significant challenge for financial institutions. Once funds leave the traditional banking system and enter cryptocurrency networks, tracing their ultimate holder can become difficult. However, the movement of money across different accounts and platforms can also provide valuable intelligence. Such transaction patterns may help identify links to fraudulent activities. Sanyal also emphasised the importance of collaboration between agencies, including initiatives involving the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), to identify suspicious patterns and connect information from different sources. How your behaviour could reveal a financial scam. Behavioural analysis is emerging as another layer of fraud detection, helping financial institutions look beyond conventional security measures such as passwords and one-time passwords (OTPs). Sanyal referred to what are known as BioCatch signals. These systems analyse how individuals interact with their devices while conducting financial transactions. This can include typing patterns, the pressure or speed of interaction and even changes in eye movement. Book ‘Banking in a New World’ examines emerging technologies, geopolitical shifts and sustainability trends transforming financial services. City Air News Nov 23, 2026 11:07 0. Facebook. Twitter. Chandigarh, November 23, 2026: Artificial intelligence, blockchain, digital currencies and sustainability are fundamentally reshaping the global banking sector, said senior banker and author Sandeep Sethi at the launch of his book, Banking in a New World, at Chandigarh Club on Monday. The book was launched in the presence of former IAS officer Vivek Atray and prominent members of the banking, business and professional communities. Speaking on the occasion, Atray, author of Not So Randomly Yours, said Sethi’s extensive international experience offered valuable practical insights into the rapidly evolving banking landscape. He said the book was highly relevant in helping readers understand changes in the financial sector and prepare for emerging opportunities and challenges. Drawing on over three decades of experience in financial services, including more than 20 years in Hong Kong, Sethi explores the forces driving transformation in banking. These include fintech, the digital-first economy, environmental, social and governance (ESG) priorities, changing wealth patterns, geopolitical fragmentation and artificial intelligence. The book also features insights from global banking, fintech and corporate practitioners, examining how financial institutions are adapting to technological advances and what the future of banking may look like. Sethi spent 27 years with a leading global bank, holding senior positions in corporate banking, transaction banking and operations. In 2020, he was named Best Relationship Manager by The Asset magazine, becoming the first and only recipient of the award across Asia-Pacific that year. Currently, he serves on the board of the Fintech Association of Hong Kong and is International Resource Director and Contributing Editor at The Asian Banker. The book is aimed at banking professionals, business leaders and readers interested in technology and the future of global finance. Tags:. Banking Technology. Artificial Intelligence. Blockchain.
